problems: The blind guess reads the silhouette as a standing human, not a gull. The blue outline has a head at top, arms out to the sides, and two legs splayed down to the feet at about (180,380) and (243,378). Nothing reads as a bird in flight.

The left and right wings are not wing shapes. The left wing is a thin arm-like line from the neck to 765 at (132,264). The right side runs from the shoulder 114421 at (315,240) to the wingtip 112122 at (399,273), then bends back down to 112623 at (374,350). That bend looks like an elbow and forearm, not a trailing wing edge.
The tail fork 117315 at (210,332) sits low between two leg-like lobes, so it reads as a hip or crotch rather than a tail.
The blue outline has no clear head, beak or neck. The head is a narrow rod, and 116231 at (236,108) only reads as a point at the top.

Gold lines form a stick figure: head to neck to breast, breast to 765, breast to shoulder, shoulder to wingtip, wingtip to trailing corner, and breast to tail fork. They match the human reading and are not a bird.
Labels overlap. 'right wing shoulder' runs into 'breast, centre of the body', and 'left wingtip' sits on the blue outline.
Stars are roughly on the intended parts, but the figure they outline is wrong. The star placement is not the problem.
output.advice:
Redraw the silhouette as a gull in flight, not a standing figure. Keep the stars where they are and change the shape around them.

1. Body: run a horizontal-ish body from the head to the tail. Head 116231 at (236,108) is the front; the beak tip is at its top. Neck 116389 at (234,195) is a short, thick connector. Breast 116602 at (230,247) is the centre of the body. Tail fork 117315 at (210,332) should sit behind the body, pulled back so the body runs head-to-tail roughly along the gold line from (236,108) to (210,332). Draw a forked tail there, with two tips spreading from the fork.

2. Right wing: draw a long, swept wing from the shoulder 114421 at (315,240) out to the tip 112122 at (399,273). Make the leading edge run straight from the shoulder to the tip, and the trailing edge run back from the tip toward the body. Place 112623 at (374,350) on the trailing edge, about two-thirds of the way back toward the body. The trailing edge should curve from the tip, through 112623, and back to the breast. Do not let it bend into an elbow.

3. Left wing: draw the matching wing from the breast/shoulder area out to 765 at (132,264). Make it a broad, tapered wing shape, not a thin rod. Its trailing edge should come back toward the tail fork.

4. Remove the legs entirely: delete the outline lobes that drop below the tail fork toward (180,380) and (243,378). A gull has no legs in flight.

5. Labels: move 'right wing shoulder' so it does not overlap 'breast, centre of the body', and move 'left wingtip' off the outline.

Check the result: the head should be clearly the front, a forked tail at the back, and two wings spread out to the sides. It should not read as arms and legs.
